sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Listen to a podcast or lecture for two minutes. What was the speaker’s attitude, not just the topic?
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Advanced listening means hearing stance, implication and structure, not only individual words.

blocks.text: Speakers signal attitude through intonation, modal particles and hedging: “Das ist ja interessant”, “Das dürfte schwierig werden”, “Man könnte meinen …”. These cues often matter more than the literal content.

Take notes in a structure: main claim, supporting points, examples and open questions. Do not transcribe. If you miss a word, use the context to infer it and keep listening; stopping at every unknown word destroys comprehension.

blocks.title: Listen for the verb, not every noun
blocks.text: In long German sentences, the final verb often carries the meaning. Train yourself to hold the sentence open until the verb arrives.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Die Haltung der Sprecherin ist skeptisch.

items: “Haltung” means stance or attitude; “Anspielung” means allusion.
Use “im Zusammenhang” to describe context: im Zusammenhang mit der Reform.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Die Haltung der Sprecherin ist skeptisch.
Die Anspielung auf die Wahl war deutlich.
items.en: The allusion to the election was clear.

items.de: Das impliziert, dass die Reform noch nicht beschlossen ist.
items.en: That implies that the reform has not yet been decided.
What exactly do you mean by that?

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

blocks.text: German discussion programmes often feature overlapping speech and rapid turn-taking. Learning to follow the argument, not every word, is essential.
Politicians and officials may use cautious language to avoid commitment. Phrases such as “Das ist derzeit nicht vorgesehen” are often softer than a direct no.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: A journalist asks a politician about a reform.

lines.speaker: Journalistin
lines.en: Is the reform still on schedule?

lines.speaker: Politiker

lines.speaker: Journalistin

lines.speaker: Politiker

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Hedging and stance
sections.lede: Modal verbs, particles and adverbs carry the speaker’s attitude.

blocks.text: “Ja” as a modal particle does not mean yes. In “Das ist ja interessant”, it signals surprise or irony. Listen for the tone, not the dictionary meaning.

sections.tip: After each listening, write one sentence about the speaker’s attitude. If you cannot, listen again for the cues.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Describe a speaker’s stance and one implicit message you heard.

model.de: Die Haltung der Sprecherin ist skeptisch. Sie sagt, die Reform dürfte schwierig werden. Das impliziert, dass sie mit einer Verzögerung rechnet.
model.en: The speaker’s stance is sceptical. She says the reform is likely to be difficult. That implies that she expects a delay.

tips: Describe stance with an adjective: skeptisch, optimistisch, zurückhaltend.
Use “Das impliziert, dass …” to name the implicit message.
Support your reading with one phrase you actually heard.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Die Haltung von der Sprecherin ist skeptisch.
items.right: Die Haltung der Sprecherin ist skeptisch.
items.why: The genitive is der Sprecherin; von is unnecessary and less formal here.

items.wrong: Das impliziert, dass die Reform ist nicht beschlossen.
items.right: Das impliziert, dass die Reform nicht beschlossen ist.
items.why: The dass-clause puts the verb at the end.
The fixed phrase is mit etwas meinen.
